title: Oscar and the Sigil
premise: Hazel Voss, a royal food-taster whose body is a ledger of poisons survived, discovers her own name and tonight's date in a century-old book of prophecies — and the prophecy begins rewriting the world around her. She and Oscar Quill, a guild archivist who trades in impossible things, learn that their country of Vell was erased from history by a sigil carved into its founding stone, and only two people anchored outside time can walk out through a door that no longer exists. As the erasure spreads street by street, Hazel must choose between drinking the final poison that will make her immune to the sigil's pull and keeping the memories that make her herself. In the end they find the door inside each other: Oscar sacrifices his name to the sigil so Hazel can carry theirs across, and she rebuilds Vell from memory, one dish at a time.
about_author: Dominic Winterbourne is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing documents from countries that no longer appear on maps. They write fantasy about people whose jobs are too small for the worlds that collapse around them.

chapters.title: The Taster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She catalogs tonight's court banquet in her poison-immunity ledger while secretly balancing accounts for the Guild of Impossible Things, where she trades favors with archivist Oscar Quill. A quiet chapter establishing her double life, her careful survival, and the warmth she hides behind professional detachment.

chapters.title: A Date Written in Ash
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Restocking the guild's archive, he finds a prophecy book dated a century past, its ink still wet, naming Hazel, himself, and tonight. He tells himself it's a forgery even as the shelf rearranges around it. The beat is dread disguised as curiosity.

chapters.title: The Banquet That Wasn't
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the royal banquet she tastes hemlock in the king's cup — but when she looks up, the hall is empty, the candles unlit, and the prophecy book lies open on the dais. The world stutters like a skipped heartbeat. Fear arrives before understanding.

chapters.title: Streets With No Names
chapters.summary: Oscar and Hazel together. They flee the palace into a city whose street signs are blanking, whose citizens forget mid-sentence. The guildhall is the last fixed point. The emotional beat: two guarded people forced to trust each other as the ground of reality softens.

chapters.title: What the Guild Sells
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. He reveals the guild's true inventory: impossible things — yesterday's rain, a dead man's shadow, doors out of closed countries. The master ledger shows Vell was sold once before, a hundred years ago, and someone has bought it back. Betrayal seeds itself in him.

chapters.title: The Founding Stone
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Beneath the ruined cathedral they find the founding stone bearing the Sigil of Erasure, half-carved, waiting. Touching it, Hazel hears her mother's voice reciting the prophecy. She realizes her bloodline wrote it. Grief and inheritance entwine.

chapters.title: Immunity Is a Kind of Wound
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, intimate and slow. She reviews her ledger: every poison survived left a scar, a tolerance, a small death. The sigil cannot erase what has already died and returned. Her survival becomes the key — and the trap. The beat is bitter self-recognition.

chapters.title: The Buyer
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The buyer appears: a faceless broker wearing the guild's old seal, offering Oscar his heart's price — restoration of his erased brother — if he hands over Hazel. Oscar refuses aloud but does not say no. Guilt becomes a second antagonist.

chapters.title: Recipes for Remembering
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hiding in a fading bakery, she cooks her grandmother's dishes, and the smells hold the neighborhood together a few hours longer. Neighbors gather, remembering. Love against duty crystallizes: memory is something you feed people.

chapters.title: The Door That No Longer Exists
chapters.summary: Together. The guild opens the exit door — but it opens onto nothing, because Vell no longer exists to be exited from. The door needs an anchor outside time. Oscar confesses the broker's offer; Hazel forgives him before he finishes asking. Trust, tested and kept.

chapters.title: Prophecy's Fine Print
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Rereading the prophecy, he finds the clause everyone missed: only one may leave; the other becomes the new anchor holding Vell's ghost together. He hides the page. The beat is the quiet rot of a secret told to oneself.

chapters.title: The King Who Forgot Himself
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They find the king wandering his empty throne room, having forgotten his own name but not his hunger. Hazel feeds him; he remembers enough to give her the royal seal — the second key to the door. Dignity in dissolution; a small coronation of kindness.

chapters.title: Erasure Comes for the Guild
chapters.summary: Together, action-heavy. The broker's agents blank the guildhall shelf by shelf. Oscar burns the impossible inventory to buy time, weeping over each loss. Hazel drags him out as the building forgets its own walls. Sacrifice as momentum.

chapters.title: What Hazel Cannot Taste
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She realizes she no longer tastes salt — the sigil is eating her senses one by one, starting with what she loves most. She writes her recipes into her skin with needle and ink. The beat: defiance rendered as body horror turned devotion.

chapters.title: The Broker's Bargain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Confronted alone, Oscar learns the broker is the first anchor — a person who chose to stay and became the sigil's hand. The offer returns, sweeter: stay, and his brother lives in the remembered Vell. Oscar says yes. The betrayal lands.

chapters.title: Two Keys, One Lock
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the door with the seal and her blood-ink, Hazel waits, and Oscar comes not to stop her but to open the far side — he never intended to keep her; he traded himself. The page he hid falls from his coat. Fury, then understanding, then grief.

chapters.title: The Last Poison
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. To pass through, she must drink the final entry in her ledger — a draught distilled from Vell itself — dying to the country so she can carry it. She drinks at the threshold with Oscar's hand in hers. The beat is love expressed as letting go.

chapters.title: The Anchor's Name
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. The sigil completes itself; the broker moves to seal the door forever. Oscar speaks his true name into the stone, unmaking the broker's claim and binding himself as anchor. Hazel crosses as Vell goes dark behind her. Maximum cost, maximum clarity.

chapters.title: A Country Carried in a Body
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, aftermath. She wakes beyond the border in a foreign inn, tasting salt again — Vell's flavor living in her tongue. She is the last citizen, the ledger, the archive. The beat is hollow survival asking what it was for.

chapters.title: Cooking a Country Back
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. She opens a tiny kitchen in the border town and cooks Vell's dishes for refugees and travelers, and those who eat remember fragments — a street, a song, a king's laugh. Memory proves contagious. Hope rebuilt as daily labor.

chapters.title: The Door in the Pantry
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Behind her flour shelf, a hairline crack of light: Oscar's anchor holds, and through it his voice, patient as a held breath. Each night she cooks a dish and passes it through. Love against duty resolved — she keeps both, imperfectly.

chapters.title: Oscar and the Sigil
chapters.summary: Final chapter, dual POV. On the centenary of the erasure, Hazel walks through the pantry door carrying a country's worth of cooked memory, and the sigil, fed a hundred years of remembrance instead of forgetting, releases its anchor. Oscar steps out nameless; Hazel gives him hers to borrow. Vell reappears on no map but every table. Resolution: identity is shared, survival is a recipe, and the door stays open.
